title: Agentic Postgres connector
description: One connector a project publishes (ADR 0236): WHAT it does -- the event an outbound connector delivers, or the definition an inbound or scheduled connector starts and the input it starts it with. Never WHERE: an outbound connector's endpoint is a per-deployment value in the project manifest's `connectors.endpoints` (D1786), because a committed file is shared by every deployment of its set. This schema is the shape; `connector_definition.compile` is the meaning, and it refuses a member of another kind by name.

schema_version.description: 1, the only version. A connector is installed as a row and is immutable per (name, version) except for its endpoint, so a second schema version is a decision about migrating rows.

name.description: The connector's name, unique across the project: `app_private.connector.name`'s CHECK, the key of its endpoint in the manifest, and the last segment of an inbound connector's route `POST /connectors/{name}`.

version.description: The connector's version. The same (name, version) with a different source refuses the deploy (PT409); a higher version that changes what the connector does is installed DISABLED and unbound, because the agent an administrator bound was bound to the old one.

description.description: What this connector is for, in the author's own words.

kind.description: `outbound` delivers an event to this deployment's endpoint (ADR 0238); `inbound` starts a run of a definition from a signed request (ADR 0237); `scheduled` starts one on an interval (ADR 0236).

event.description: Outbound only. The event delivered, as `name@version` -- `app.emit_event`'s name rule and a version always.

retry.description: Outbound only. How many times a delivery is retried after its first attempt, and how long it waits between attempts. The table's own bounds.

workflow.description: Inbound and scheduled only. The definition started, as `name@version`, which must be a definition in the SAME set's `workflows/` at that version. The connector records that definition's required scopes, and the agent an administrator binds must hold exactly those.

body.description: Inbound only. The request body, in a CLOSED subset (ADR 0237, D1787): named members, no nesting, nothing undeclared. The body IS the run's input, so every member must be one the definition references as `{{input.<member>}}` and every such reference must be a member.

schedule.description: Scheduled only. The interval, from the moment an administrator enables it; missed fires coalesce to one.

input.description: Scheduled only. The run's input: literals, exactly the keys the definition references as `{{input.<key>}}`.

member.description: One body member. A string declares its `max_length`; an integer its `minimum` and `maximum`; a boolean neither.
